subject: Re: Pilot packaging options — top-up vs short convert for HelixWorks
messages:
From: Alicia Ramirez <alicia@helixworks.com>
To: jasmine liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Timothy Cho <timothy.cho@helixworks.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot runway — need short extension or credit top-up

Hi Jasmine,

Quick note from our engineering lead: we're hitting the token cap on our 4-week pilot faster than expected because we ran a burst of ingest/embedding tests. Procurement is tied up but the team needs another ~3 weeks of the same environment to finish validation.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood either (A) extend the existing timebox for 3 weeks as a one-off addendum, or (B) sell a short top-up (hours/credits) we can charge against immediately?
- If we convert to a paid pilot or commit within 30 days after the extension, would you be able to apply any of the top-up spend as a credit toward the first month?

Attached is an updated SOW that shows the final test plan and target metrics. Procurement also asked for a simple pricing comparison — is there a short breakdown you can share?

Thanks,
Alicia Ramirez
Head of ML Ops
HelixWorks

[Attachment: HelixWorks_SOW_v2.docx (docx)]

From: jasmine liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Ramirez <alicia@helixworks.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Apr 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot runway — need short extension or credit top-up

Thanks for the context, Alicia — glad to hear the burst yielded useful signal. We can do both options; I wanted to lay out practical differences so you have what procurement needs. Short summary below, then a recommended path based on common outcomes.

Option A — Timebox extension (recommended if you want no billing changes):
- 3-week extension of the existing pilot environment
- Flat fee: $18,000 (covers sustained hosted inference capacity sized to current pilot config)
- Includes same SLAs and support level; no change to model or region
- Pros: simplest for engineering; keeps environment identical
- Cons: non-refundable, not applied automatically to future commit unless we agree to a conversion credit in writing

Option B — Credit top-up (recommended if you may convert early):
- Purchase token/compute credits: $5,000 per 100k token-equivalent / or equivalent 150 GPU hours (short-burst SKU)
- Credits billed now, consumed as you run (we'll provide meter with token and hour breakdown)
- If you convert to a monthly commit within 30 days of purchase, we can apply up to 50% of unused top-up as a dollar-for-dollar credit toward month 1 (subject to a signed amendment)
- Pros: flexible, partially convertible; cons: requires procurement to approve purchase order

Option C — Convert to a short-term committed starter (if you expect steady throughput):
- 3-month starter commit: $40k/mo list -> 15% pilot conversion discount if we sign within 10 days
- Pros: best unit economics and predictable capacity; cons: procurement paperwork/time

Attachments: quick pricing sheet for the three options (pricing-sheet-Q2.pdf). If procurement needs, Ben can propose a short mutual action plan / MAP we typically use to speed approvals.

My recommendation: If procurement can authorize a PO quickly, go with Option B (top-up) so you don’t change the environment and we keep conversion flexibility. If you need zero procurement changes, Option A is fastest.

I can put a 48-hour hold on the $18k extension and the top-up pricing while we confirm. What does procurement need from our side to approve a PO?

— Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: pricing-sheet-Q2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Alicia Ramirez <alicia@helixworks.com>
To: jasmine liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Apr 2025 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot runway — need short extension or credit top-up

Thanks, Jasmine — that framing helps. A couple of quick clarifying q's from procurement and our finance lead:
1) If we buy the credit top-up and then convert, you noted "up to 50% of unused top-up" — can that be pushed to 75% for chance-to-convert customers (we're a strategic target for a 2026 broader rollout)?
2) Does the credit apply to Dedicated pricing? We may test dedicated in parallel after the pilot.
3) Are you able to invoice to a PO and accept Net30?

Tim (cc) is the procurement lead — Tim, any constraints on PO timing?

Cheers,
Alicia

Looping in Marissa to confirm commercial flexibility. Alicia — happy to accelerate here and give HelixWorks a slightly enhanced convert credit given your roadmap. Proposed hybrid:
- 150 GPU-hour top-up pack (burst SKU) priced at $4,700 (10% discount vs list)
- If Helix converts to a paid monthly commit within 30 days, Redwood will apply 75% of any *unused* top-up dollars as a credit toward month 1 (we'll track usage and provide a reconciliation report)
- If Helix moves to Dedicated within 60 days, we can apply 50% of unused top-up as credit against the Dedicated onboarding invoice (not ongoing monthly list)
- We can invoice to a PO with Net30; for larger commits we'll need standard SOW and signature (happy to share a templated amendment)

Next step: I can send a 1-page mutual action plan (MAP) that lists dates, who signs what, and the PO amount — that usually helps procurement move quickly. Marissa — please confirm CX/finance approval on the 75% convert credit and the 10% top-up discount.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

- Offer: 150 GPU-hour top-up pack (burst SKU) — $4,700 (invoiceable to PO, Net30)
- Convert credit: 75% of any *unused* top-up dollars applied as credit to month 1 if Helix signs a monthly commit within 30 days of invoice date
- Dedicated path: if Helix elects Dedicated within 60 days, 50% of unused top-up dollars apply to the onboarding invoice
- Expiration: this offer and the 75% convert-credit window expires 7 days from this email
- Execution: please sign the attached one-page amendment and return — or click the DocuSign link below to execute.

DocuSign: https://app.redwood.ai/docusign/HLX-2025-04

If you want, we can also do a 2-week timebox extension flat quote for $11,000 instead (no conversion credits) — picking that option just speeds delivery faster if procurement doesn't want extra line items.
